title: Companies Act, 2013 — Section 378C (Formation of Producer Company and its registration)

content.overview: Any ten or more individuals, each being a producer, or any two or more Producer Institutions, or a combination of ten or more individuals and Producer Institutions, may form an incorporated company as a Producer Company having objects specified in section 378B. On registration the company becomes a body corporate as if it is a private limited company to which Chapter XXIA applies, without limit on the number of Members, and it shall never become or be deemed a public limited company.
content.glance: Minimum promoters: 10 individual producers, or 2 Producer Institutions, or a combination; limited by shares; never a public company.
content.study: Section 378C sets the formation threshold and registration process. The Registrar, if satisfied, registers the memorandum, articles and other documents and issues a certificate of incorporation within thirty days. Liability of Members is limited by the memorandum to the amount unpaid on their shares. Promoters may be reimbursed direct promotion and registration costs subject to approval at the first general meeting. The resulting Producer Company is treated as a private limited company for the purposes of the Chapter but has no membership ceiling and cannot become public.

sections.heading: Rule
sections.body: Ten or more individual producers, or two or more Producer Institutions, or a combination, may form a Producer Company with objects under s. 378B; on registration it is limited by shares and never becomes public.

examples.title: Illustration — s. 378C
examples.body: Twelve farmers and one Producer Institution incorporate a Producer Company under s. 378C with objects confined to s. 378B.

hypotheticals.question: What is the core effect of s. 378C?
hypotheticals.analysis: It fixes who may form a Producer Company, the registration process, limited liability and the permanent private-company character.

misconceptions.trap: Assuming ordinary private-company membership limits apply.
misconceptions.correction: A Producer Company has no membership ceiling and cannot become public.
